result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of being wrong.

Not just in science or debate, but in every conversation, every relationship, every institution. Fear of being wrong silences voices, stifles innovation, and entrenches dogma. It turns curiosity into caution, creativity into compliance, and growth into stagnation.

Imagine a world where people could say, *"I don’t know,"* without shame. Where mistakes were not stigmatized but celebrated as the raw material of progress. Where listening was as valued as speaking, and where the pursuit of truth—even an uncomfortable one—was the highest virtue.

That fear is the root of so much division: the refusal to admit ignorance, the stubbornness of ideology, the cruelty of certainty. If we could unlearn it, we might finally start solving the problems we’ve been too afraid to face.
